title: Sandbox probes cannot clearly distinguish vector credential failures from queue saturation
wanted_capability: During sandbox observability probes, vector degradation should expose a clear, current per-route reason so agents can tell whether hybrid search is degraded by missing credentials, queue saturation, stale retry errors, or empty corpus coverage without guessing from mixed messages.
missing_primitive: current normalized vector-degradation reason in bbox_hybrid_search / bbox_embed_status
fallback_used: Compared bbox_hybrid_search degradation text from probes with bbox_embed_status; inferred that most Voyage routes are available, code is queue-full, and notes still reports an older key-missing retry error.
evidence: bbox_embed_status: code available=false queue_depth=10000 last_error='embedding route queue full'
bbox_embed_status: notes available=false last_error='VOYAGE_API_KEY or DAYSTROM_VOYAGE_API_KEY is required' while other Voyage routes are available
probe bc8d9fef: hybrid search reported degraded vector route/API key unavailable
probe ef008f5c: hybrid search reported degraded vector route while fallback remained usable
resolution_note: Addressed in the sandbox-observability MCP surface: embedding RouteStatus now includes normalized health and health_reason fields; bbox_embed_status returns them after coverage merge; bbox_hybrid_search renders unhealthy route health summaries. Validation: cargo test -p blackbox route_health_classifies_common_failure_reasons --lib; cargo test -p blackbox render_text_names_unhealthy_vector_route_reasons --lib; cargo test -p blackbox tool_docs --lib; isolated debug daemon bbox_embed_status showed health/health_reason on every route; isolated Brodex probe aa892bee and retro 6b2a3d9f reported the surface visible/actionable with friction none.
